subject: Post-call: capacity assurance & POC next steps (dedicated vs hyperscaler)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-11T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: capacity assurance & POC next steps (dedicated vs hyperscaler)

Hi Sarah — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Recap from our call:
- AcmeCloud is evaluating dedicated reserved capacity vs hyperscaler reserved GPUs + burst/spot for inference.
- Primary success criteria: p95 latency < 120ms for 2k tokens, sustained throughput 200 qps, predictable tail latency during traffic spikes, and clear capacity guarantees for peak retail events.
- Procurement timeline: you are aiming for a decision in 6–8 weeks, procurement owner TBD.

What we propose for the POC (attachments): capacity_test_plan.xlsx (detailed scripts) and SLA_comparison.pdf
POC phases and acceptance criteria (high-level):
1) Baseline: run your production prompts against Redwood-hosted model variant for 48h to profile token distribution and cold-start behavior.
2) Stress / sustained run: 6h sustained 200 qps to validate warm KV-cache and batching behavior; measure p50/p95/p99 latency and token cost.
3) Preemption/failure sim: simulate a node drain and confirm failover to warm regional pool within target RTO (we recommend target 60s).
4) Burst scenario: validate auto-burst policies and cold-start impact when scaling from 0->200 qps in <2 minutes.
5) Quality delta check: compare outputs for quantized model variant (4-bit) vs fp16 to ensure accuracy within your tolerance.

Key Redwood differentiators to highlight in evaluation:
- Dedicated reserved pools with explicit SLOs and automated fallback to compatible variants (we return to a pinned model only after rollout completes).
- Smart routing by policy (latency vs cost) so you can route non-critical workloads to lower-cost variants.
- Prefix/KV cache and continuous batching tuned to your token distribution to reduce per-token cost without pushing up p95.

Ask from you by EOD Friday: confirm the procurement contact and whether Acme can share a representative prompt set (anonymized) so we can parameterize tests.

Proposed timeline:
- This week: exchange procurement contact + test data
- Next week: run baseline profiling (48h)
- Week after: stress/preemption/burst runs and deliver results + runbook

Attachments: capacity_test_plan.xlsx (xlsx), SLA_comparison.pdf (pdf)

Thanks — I’ll loop in Evelyn to scope the test harness.

—Ben
Ben Carter | Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0186
Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@acmecloud.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Platform Team <platform-team@acmecloud.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T11:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: capacity assurance & POC next steps (dedicated vs hyperscaler)

Thanks Ben — appreciate the clear summary. A few clarifying items from our side: 

1) Procurement & pricing asks:
- Our procurement lead (copying in next note once I confirm) wants to understand reserved commitments: minimum term options (3/6/12/24 months) and whether Redwood offers pro-rated evaluation windows prior to full commit.
- Also need clear language on SLA credits for sustained downtime and an example remedy timeline.

2) Competitive note: we’re also running parallel conversations with a hyperscaler (reserved GPUs + burst to preemptible). Their pitch is lower sticker price for reserved units but with less predictable preemption during peak events. Can Redwood provide an apples-to-apples cost + SLO comparison for a 12-month commit?

3) Test data: yes, we can share an anonymized prompt set. I attached our internal_requirements.pdf that lists operational thresholds and audit evidence we’ll require (SOC2 logs, request-level latency traces, and billing granularity).

4) Team availability: we can start baseline profiling as early as Mon next week.

If you can include a short section in the POC plan that maps test results to procurement decision gates (e.g., pass/fail thresholds for moving to committed capacity), that will help accelerate approval.

—Sarah
Sarah Lin
Director, Platform Engineering | AcmeCloud
sarah.lin@acmecloud.com
Attachment: internal_requirements.pdf
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Platform Team <platform-team@acmecloud.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T13:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: capacity assurance & POC next steps (dedicated vs hyperscaler)

Thanks Sarah — great, we’ll proceed on that timeline. A few notes to address your asks and map expectations for procurement: 

Reserved commitment options and evaluation windows:
- We support 3/6/12/24 month reserved capacity contracts. For evaluations, we can offer a 30-day pro-rated trial on reserved units (you pay for use above credits) to validate throughput and tail behavior before full term billing kicks in.
- Example: 12-month commit with a 30-day trial; if you convert, month 1 is pro-rated and the commit is amortized over the remaining term.

SLA language (high level):
- We provide SLOs for availability and tail latency with a credit schedule for violations. For POC we can provide sample SLA text and an example credit calculation tied to missed p95 targets.

Competitive comparison (we’ll attach to final POC results):
- Hyperscaler reserved GPUs: lower raw hourly price, but higher variability due to preemption and cold-start cost when relying on spot/burst patterns.
- Redwood Dedicated: slightly higher committed price but includes reserved GPU pools, faster failover (regional pools + warm KV cache), and deterministic routing policies that reduce unexpected tail latency.

Technical POC scope (what we can run for you):
- Baseline profiling (48h) + stress run (6h sustained at target QPS) + preemption sim (node drain) + burst ramp test.
- Deliverables: metrics pack (p50/p95/p99), token cost breakdown, traces (sample spans), and a short cost model comparing the two options at your expected traffic profile.

Attachments added: redwood-poc-checklist.md, test-scenarios.sh (script)

Next steps:
- Sarah: please send the anonymized prompt set + procurement contact.
- Our team: start baseline profiling Mon and share initial report Wed next week.

Looping in Evelyn to confirm test harness and logging outputs we’ll provide. Evelyn — can your team confirm we can provide per-request trace IDs and billing granularity down to 1-minute buckets?

—Ben
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-11T15:49:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Re: Post-call: capacity assurance & POC next steps (dedicated vs hyperscaler)

Vivek — forwarding the Acme thread and proposed POC scope. TL;DR: Acme will run baseline + stress + preemption + burst. They want an apples-to-apples cost/SLO comparison with their hyperscaler option and procurement will want sample SLA language.

Acceptance criteria I recommend we commit to for the POC report:
- p95 < 120ms for 2k-token median prompt during sustained run
- Failover RTO < 60s on node drain with no request failures > 10s
- Cost model: show cost per 1M tokens for (a) reserved 12-month commit, (b) committed + burst policy, (c) hyperscaler reserved+spot mix
- Deliver per-request trace IDs and 1-minute billing granularity for auditability

Commercial ask from Acme: they may push for a discount in exchange for a 12-month commit. My recommendation: we can offer up to 20% off list for a true 12-month reserved commitment if legal approves a standard SLA and an operational readiness checklist sign-off.

Ben/Evelyn notes below (quoted):
> On 2027-04-11T13:03:00-07:00, Ben Carter wrote:
> > We support 3/6/12/24 month reserved capacity contracts. For evaluations, we can offer a 30-day pro-rated trial on reserved units...
> > For POC deliverables: metrics pack, token cost breakdown, traces (sample spans), and cost model.

Can we approve the commercial flexibility (20% off for 12 months) to help close this one? If yes I’ll prepare the POC infra plan and handoff to solutions infra to run stress scenarios.

—Evelyn
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
